gen.orderNote: Steps follow the order described on the page from proposal to certification.

steps.label: Congress votes to propose amendment
steps.quote: an amendment may be proposed either by the Congress with a two-thirds majority vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate

steps.label: Proposal is written as joint resolution
steps.quote: The Congress proposes an amendment in the form of a joint resolution.

steps.label: Archivist notifies governors for consideration
steps.quote: The Archivist submits the proposed amendment to the States for their consideration by sending a letter of notification to each Governor

steps.label: States return proof of ratification action
steps.quote: When a State ratifies a proposed amendment, it sends the Archivist an original or certified copy of the State action

steps.label: Enough states ratify to adopt amendment
steps.quote: A proposed amendment becomes part of the Constitution as soon as it is ratified by three-fourths of the States (38 of 50 States).

steps.label: Officials draft proclamation certifying validity
steps.quote: When the OFR verifies that it has received the required number of authenticated ratification documents, it drafts a formal proclamation
